title: What he learned from each artist; John Collins
summary: Callender says he learned something from every musician and discusses John Collins's grasp of chord structure.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Did you learn anything in particular from any one of these artists?
I learned something from every one of them.

Can you give me an example of something? I ask this, because Dizzy once told me that one of his greatest musical lessons came from John Collins, which was an interesting. Sometimes something becomes very significant.
Well, John Collins' conception of chord structure anybody can learn. All you have to do is listen. John Collins is a marvelous musician. On the way over here,

I was listening to an album, a Nat King Cole album that Billy May had done the music for, and that's when John Collins and Lee Young and...I can't think of the bass player's name...Johnny Harris, I think...
